findings.evidence: The old guard `if not tags` covers both `None` and `[]` (both falsy). The replacement `if tags is None` only covers `None`. The function signature accepts `list[str] | None`, so an empty list is a valid input. When `tags=[]`, execution falls through to `tags[0].strip().lower()` on line 3, which raises `IndexError: list index out of range`.
findings.recommendation: Keep the original guard `if not tags` to handle both `None` and empty lists, or explicitly check both: `if tags is None or len(tags) == 0`.

summary: The change narrows the guard from `if not tags` to `if tags is None`, which removes protection against empty lists. When `tags=[]`, the function will now reach `tags[0]` and raise an `IndexError` instead of returning `None`.
